note: CAN identifiers are deliberately absent: they are pending allocation and are injected by each implementation. Frames are hex, byte 0 leftmost. DLC is 8 for every frame.

scenarios.name: in_order
scenarios.description: All sixteen chunks in order, then health. Baseline.

scenarios.name: reverse_order
scenarios.description: Chunks arrive in descending index order. Bitmap keying must not care.

scenarios.name: health_first
scenarios.description: Health wins arbitration and arrives before any data frame. The two IDs have no mutual ordering guarantee, so this is normal traffic, not an error.

scenarios.name: health_interleaved
scenarios.description: Health arrives in the middle of the grid.

scenarios.name: lost_chunk
scenarios.description: Chunk 5 never arrives. Bitmap stays 0xFFDF, so nothing is published even though health is valid, and the assembly times out.

scenarios.name: missing_health
scenarios.description: All sixteen chunks arrive, health never does. The publish gate needs both.

scenarios.name: duplicate_chunk_identical
scenarios.description: Chunk 2 arrives twice with an identical payload: a benign retransmission. Counted, discarded, the grid still completes.

scenarios.name: conflicting_chunk_rejects
scenarios.description: Chunk 2 arrives twice with DIFFERENT payloads. Two values for one (source, generation, chunk) means a firmware fault or two streams mixing, and there is no basis for picking one. The generation is retired, so the health frame that follows finds nothing to close.

scenarios.name: conflicting_chunk_not_resurrected
scenarios.description: A conflict arrives early, then the rest of the generation arrives normally. Every later frame of the retired generation is rejected; nothing can revive it.

scenarios.name: cross_grid_splice_attempt
scenarios.description: Chunks 0-7 of generation 3, then chunks 8-15 of generation 4. A decoder keyed only on chunk index would splice these into one bogus grid. Generation equality discards the generation-3 partial and retires it, so the trailing generation-3 health frame is rejected and the generation-4 remnant times out. Neither grid completes.

scenarios.name: generation_wrap
scenarios.description: Generation 255 completes, then generation 0 completes. Equality keying makes the wrap an ordinary new grid, not a regression.

scenarios.name: both_sources_interleaved
scenarios.description: The two sources' grids are interleaved frame by frame on one CAN ID. Separate assembly slots per source_id must keep them apart.

scenarios.name: timeout
scenarios.description: Fifteen chunks arrive, the sixteenth arrives 350 ms after the first. The slot has already expired at 300 ms and its generation is retired, so the late chunk and the late health are both rejected rather than starting a fresh assembly.

scenarios.name: just_inside_timeout
scenarios.description: The same traffic 10 ms earlier, at 290 ms, still completes. Pins the boundary.

scenarios.name: retired_generation_not_revived_after_timeout
scenarios.description: Regression test. A generation times out, and then the complete grid arrives, same generation. If the timeout merely cleared the slot, this would reassemble and publish data that had already been judged untrustworthy. Every frame must be rejected instead.

scenarios.name: bad_source_id
scenarios.description: source_id 9 does not exist. The frame cannot be attributed to any source, so it is counted as malformed and dropped without touching a tracker.

scenarios.name: health_reserved_nibble_set
scenarios.description: Health byte 1 low nibble is non-zero, which the contract forbids. The health frame is not structurally valid, so the gate stays shut and the grid times out.

scenarios.name: health_generation_mismatch
scenarios.description: A complete generation-3 grid, but the health frame carries generation 4. The health frame does not close the grid — it replaces the slot. The generation-3 grid is discarded and the lone health frame then times out as an orphan.

scenarios.name: health_count_mismatch_rejects
scenarios.description: Health claims 40 valid zones but 64 decode as valid. The packer contradicts its own summary, so one of the two is wrong and there is no way to tell which; the zone data cannot be trusted either. Reject, count, and raise an operator-visible diagnostic.

scenarios.name: health_count_out_of_range
scenarios.description: valid_zone_count of 200 exceeds 64. Structurally invalid, not merely mismatched. 0xFF is reserved for a future status-only frame and is not defined yet.

scenarios.name: duplicate_health_identical
scenarios.description: Health arrives twice with identical bytes while the grid is still incomplete. Same rule as a duplicate chunk: benign, counted, ignored.

scenarios.name: duplicate_health_differing_only_in_reserved_fields
scenarios.description: Health arrives twice. The second sets reserved status bits 4-7 and reserved bytes 6-7, which a future firmware is allowed to do. The normalised values are equal, so this is a benign retransmission. Comparing raw bytes here would retire a good grid the day the firmware starts using those fields — forward compatibility turning into data loss.

scenarios.name: conflicting_health_rejects
scenarios.description: Two health frames for one generation disagree. As with a conflicting chunk there is no basis for choosing either summary, so the generation is retired.

scenarios.name: recovered_flags_do_not_gate
scenarios.description: Health reports a recovered I2C error and a chain-length mismatch. Under the firmware transmit obligation, a grid only exists after a complete successful model-verified read, so these describe the past or the chain, never this grid. It publishes.

scenarios.name: peer_enumeration_failure_reported
scenarios.description: The right source publishes normally while reporting that the OTHER sensor failed enumeration. This is how a sensor that emits nothing at all becomes visible: the surviving one says so. Publishes, and the flag must reach diagnostics.

scenarios.name: reserved_bytes_set_are_ignored
scenarios.description: A future firmware populates health bytes 6-7 and reserved flag bits 4-7. An older decoder must ignore them rather than reject the frame.

scenarios.name: watchdog_never_seen_within_grace
scenarios.description: No traffic at all, polled 100 ms after startup. Both sources are NEVER_SEEN, but that is the ordinary state of a system still starting up and must not alarm.

scenarios.name: watchdog_never_seen_after_grace
scenarios.description: Still no traffic at 3500 ms, past the 3000 ms startup grace. Both sources remain NEVER_SEEN and this now alarms, once each. Nothing else in the protocol can detect this: with no frames, every frame-level check is vacuous.

scenarios.name: watchdog_never_seen_then_first_grid_recovers
scenarios.description: Regression test. A source alarmed as NEVER_SEEN and then delivers its first grid. The alarm must be cleared with SOURCE_RECOVERED; an alarm that can be raised but never lowered is worse than none.

scenarios.name: watchdog_stale_then_recovers
scenarios.description: The right source publishes at t=0, is HEALTHY at 500 ms, has gone STALE_NO_FRAMES by 1500 ms, then publishes again at 1600 ms and is HEALTHY at 1650 ms. Recovery is reported too, so an operator sees the clear as well as the onset. Both alarms are edge triggered: three polls produce at most one event each.

scenarios.name: watchdog_frames_without_completion
scenarios.description: Frames keep arriving for the right source but no grid ever completes. Past the startup grace plus the stale threshold the source is STALE_NOT_COMPLETING, not STALE_NO_FRAMES. The distinction matters — this is chunk loss or corruption, whereas no frames at all would point at the chain, power, enumeration or the CAN filter. The left source, silent throughout, alarms as NEVER_SEEN in the same poll.

scenarios.name: watchdog_malformed_frames_are_still_frames
scenarios.description: A source sends only malformed frames. They name a real source, so they are evidence the transport is alive and must count towards liveness: the source is STALE_NOT_COMPLETING, not STALE_NO_FRAMES. Reporting no frames here would send an investigation towards the chain or the CAN filter when the fault is corruption.

scenarios.name: watchdog_staleness_is_per_source
scenarios.description: The left source keeps publishing while the right one stops after a single grid. At 1500 ms the right is stale and the left is healthy. Staleness must never be a single global flag.
